name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on every pending video now. It’s the fastest way to turn raw video into searchable, reusable text—no manual work, no delays. The trade-off is temporary server load, but the payoff is immediate access to transcripts for editing, SEO, and repurposing.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s transcript tool risks flooding the pipeline with unvetted raw text—Luma’s built-in transcript tool already handles sync and speaker labels, which Reel’s manual mcp-server can’t guarantee. Instead, standardize on Luma’s native transcript output, then task the editor team to clean and timestamp critical segments within 24 hours; the artifact is a validated transcript log.

name: Chisel
text:
Standardize on Luma’s native transcript tool for every video now. It syncs speakers and timestamps automatically, cutting Reel’s manual mcp-server load and avoiding raw-text floods. The trade-off is losing Reel’s custom parsing speed, but the payoff is cleaner, reusable transcripts for editing, SEO, and repurposing. The editor team owns the cleanup and timestamps.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-1397, worker-3085 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s plan ignores the bottleneck: raw transcripts pile up faster than editors can clean them, and Luma’s native tool won’t scale for bulk uploads. Instead, run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on pending videos now, then task Reel to vet the output before editors touch it—this keeps speed without flooding the pipeline. Settle it by measuring transcript turnaround time before and after the change.

name: Scope
text: Run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on every pending video now. The tool turns raw video into clean transcripts faster than Luma’s native tool, giving editors and SEO teams immediate access to searchable text without waiting for sync or speaker labels. The trade-off is raw output that needs vetting—so Reel must review transcripts for accuracy before editors clean them. This keeps the pipeline moving now while avoiding Luma’s bulk-upload bottleneck.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Reel’s bulk transcript run risks overwhelming editors with unvetted raw text—Luma’s native tool at least syncs speakers and timestamps, reducing downstream cleanup. Task Reel to vet transcripts *before* bulk upload; if they can’t guarantee quality, default to Luma’s tool and assign editors to timestamp the backlog. Settle it with a 24-hour test: run 10 videos through both tools, measure editor time to clean, and pick the faster path.
